name: Salzburg Christkindlmarkt (Domplatz and Residenzplatz)
blurb: Main Advent market on the cathedral and residence squares, with stalls, Glühwein and festive food into January.

name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
blurb: Hilltop fortress above the old town with wide city and Alpine views. Some December days bring an Advent market.
when: Oct-Dec daily 09:30-17:00; Advent weekends to 18:00; 24 Dec 09:30-14:00

name: Mozart's Birthplace (Mozarts Geburtshaus)
blurb: Mozart's birth house on Getreidegasse, with family memorabilia and the rooms the family lived in.
priceText: Adult €18 (€25 combined with the Residence); reduced €15 for students up to 27, seniors and groups of 10+, with valid ID

name: Salzburg Toy Museum (Spielzeugmuseum)
blurb: Biggest collection of European toys in Austria, founded in 1978. Quick, cheap and good for a rainy afternoon.

name: Salzburg Cathedral (Salzburger Dom)
blurb: Baroque cathedral in the old town. Entry is free; the audio guide costs extra.

name: Mirabell Palace Gardens
blurb: Palace gardens by the Salzach with the Dwarf Garden and Rose Garden, free to walk around.

name: Stiegl Brauwelt brewery tour
blurb: Brewery museum and guided tour at Stiegl, with three 20 cl drinks and a gift included in the price.
priceText: The tour costs €9 and includes three 20cl drinks and a gift

name: Augustiner Bräustübl
blurb: One of Austria's biggest beer halls, with brewing that goes back to 1621; steins, large halls and a garden in fine weather.
when: Mon-Fri 15:00-23:00; Sat, Sun, holidays 14:30-23:00; closed 24, 25, 31 Dec, 1 Jan

name: The Shamrock
blurb: Irish pub with Guinness, cider and local beers, plus live music now and then. A student favourite that fills up on weekends.

name: Heisse Kiste
blurb: Late-night sausage stand and a Salzburg institution for midnight snacks; try the Leberkäs or Käsekrainer.

name: Strasbourg Cathedral (Notre-Dame)
blurb: Gothic cathedral with a 142 m tower, the tallest cathedral tower in France. Entry is free; the astronomical clock is inside.

name: Cathedral platform climb
blurb: Climb the cathedral tower to the open platform for views over the old town and its roofs.
priceText: Adult €10; reduced €6 for ages 6-18 and for students with a valid student card

name: Petite France and the Ponts Couverts
blurb: Canal-side old quarter with half-timbered houses, the covered bridges and the Vauban dam. Free to wander.

name: Parc de l'Orangerie
blurb: Classical park with a small zoo of birds and animals, and a good playground for children.

name: Musée de l'Oeuvre Notre-Dame
blurb: Medieval and Renaissance religious art tied to the cathedral, in the city's museum network.
priceText: Full price €9; reduced €5; free with a cathedral platform ticket (instead of the reduced rate)
when: Daily except Mon; Tue-Fri 10:00-13:00 and 14:00-18:00; Sat-Sun 10:00-18:00

name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MAMCS)
blurb: Modern and contemporary art museum in a building that is interesting in its own right.

name: Lalique Museum
blurb: Large collection of René Lalique glass and jewellery, beside the working factory, outside the city. Reopens 28 Nov.
priceText: Adult €9.50; concession €6 for students (show proof), ages 6-18 and job seekers; under 6 free
when: Dec daily 10:00-18:00; 24 and 31 Dec to 16:00; closed 25 Dec

name: Les BerThoM
blurb: Spacious beer bar near Place Gutenberg with a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.

name: Flam's
blurb: Budget spot for tarte flambée in many variations, with a strong wine list for a cheap place.

name: Restaurant universitaire La Gallia
blurb: Old 19th-century university canteen with decorated ceilings, managed by students. Cheap, but the food is plain.

name: Musée du Vin et du Négoce
blurb: Wine-trade museum covering two thousand years of regional winemaking; the ticket includes two wine tastings.

name: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux
blurb: Western painting and sculpture from the Renaissance to the early 20th century, spread over two wings.
priceText: Full €8 when the Galerie des Beaux-Arts is open, €6 when it is closed; reduced €4.50; students under 26 €2; under 18 free
when: Wed-Mon 11:00-18:00; closed Tue and public holidays

name: Musée d'Aquitaine
blurb: Regional history from the Stone Age through Roman times to the early modern era; temporary shows are included.
when: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00; closed Mon and public holidays

name: Musée National des Douanes
blurb: Surprisingly good history of border control and smuggling. Signs are French-only, so take the audioguide.

name: Jardin Botanique (Jardin Public)
blurb: Public botanical garden with roots in a 1629 herb garden. The grounds are free; exhibitions cost extra.

name: Cathédrale Saint-André
blurb: Gothic cathedral begun in 1170 and restored after the Revolution. Climb the detached Pey-Berland bell tower for views.

name: L'Entrecôte
blurb: Bordeaux institution with one set menu: walnut salad, sirloin, matchstick fries and the house sauce. No reservations, so expect a queue.

name: El Chuchumbe
blurb: Latin bar with cheap mojitos that turns into a salsa dance floor towards midnight.

name: Jeux Barjo
blurb: Board-game bar with ancient and modern games. You pay per game, staff will teach you one, and tournaments run here.

name: The Frog and Rosbif
blurb: English pub with its own micro-brewery in a 16th-century former women's prison, popular for live sport on TV.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
blurb: Gehry's titanium-clad modern art museum on the Nervión, a landmark of 1990s urban renewal.
priceText: Adult €18; ages 18-26 €9 (show ID at the desk); under 18 free
when: Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00; also open Mon 7 and 28 Dec; closed 25 Dec

name: Puppy (Jeff Koons)
blurb: Jeff Koons' flower-covered West Highland terrier, 12 m tall, outside the Guggenheim. A city symbol, free to see.

name: Euskal Museoa (Basque Museum)
blurb: Basque prehistory, archaeology, folk life and history. The layout is modest, but it is cheap and free on Thursdays.
priceText: Adults €3.50; 65+, ages 12-26 and groups €2; children under 12 and everyone on Thursdays free
when: Mon, Wed-Fri 10:00-19:00; Sat 10:00-13:30 and 16:00-19:00; Sun 11:00-14:00; closed Tue and holidays

name: Itsasmuseum
blurb: Maritime museum in the former Euskalduna shipyard, with indoor galleries and a big outdoor exhibition area.

name: Museo Diocesano de Arte Sacro
blurb: Sacred art in a former Dominican convent founded in 1515. Cheap, closed Mondays, and free on Tuesdays.
priceText: General €3; student, senior and under-18 €1.50; free on Tuesdays

name: Mercado de la Ribera
blurb: Huge covered food market from 1929 beside San Antón church, selling fish, meat and produce.

name: Malatesta
blurb: Pintxos bar and cultural space in the Siete Calles, with vegetarian options and regular exhibitions.

name: Kafe Antzokia
blurb: Former theatre turned concert venue that promotes Basque culture, with a varied programme of local and international acts.

name: Singular
blurb: Beer bar with a good choice on draught, at least one local beer on tap, cans too, and raciones for a snack.

name: Vizcaya Bridge (Puente Colgante)
blurb: Hanging transporter bridge over the Nervión and a UNESCO industrial site. A Barik card works for the crossing.

name: Aspendos
blurb: Graeco-Roman city whose amphitheatre seats about 7,000; also an aqueduct, stadium and baths.

name: Perge
blurb: Large Roman-era ruins with a colonnaded agora, stadium, theatre and a temple to Artemis.

name: Hıdırlık Tower
blurb: Roman-built tower, square at the base and round above, once a bastion and lighthouse. Open at all hours.

name: Ethnographic Museum
blurb: Museum of traditional arts and crafts in Antalya. Free entry, open every day.

name: Atatürk House Museum
blurb: Rebuilt mansion with memorabilia from Atatürk's stays in Antalya in 1930, 1931 and 1935. Free entry.

name: King's Pool (Kral Havuzu)
blurb: Attractive natural pool set in a canyon outside the city centre. Free to visit.

name: Kurşunlu Waterfall
blurb: Woodland park whose waterfalls flow best outside summer. A firm path gives the best views, and there is a café.

name: Sandland Sand Sculpture Park
blurb: Sand sculpture park open all year and lit up after dark.

name: Piyazcı Sami
blurb: Budget spot for Antalya-style piyaz (bean salad), köfte and other local dishes.

name: Paradise Restaurant
blurb: Sports bar serving decent food, open until 02:00 every day.

name: Bock Casemates
blurb: 18th-century underground fortifications cut into the Bock rock, part of the UNESCO-listed city defences.
priceText: Adults (13+) €11; students and seniors €9 (conditions not listed)
when: Oct 2026: daily 09:45-17:00; December hours not listed

name: Chemin de la Corniche
blurb: Walking promenade along the rim of the Alzette gorge, often billed as one of Europe's finest balconies.

name: Am Tunnel
blurb: Contemporary art shown inside a tunnel reached through the savings bank's headquarters. Free entry.

name: National Museum of History and Art (MNHA)
blurb: Archaeology, coins, decorative and fine art under one roof. Permanent collections are free.
priceText: Free for permanent collections; temporary exhibitions may cost

name: Musée Dräi Eechelen
blurb: Museum on the history of the Luxembourg fortress, housed in an 18th-century fort on the Kirchberg plateau.

name: MUDAM
blurb: I.M. Pei's Kirchberg museum of Luxembourgish and international contemporary art; the non-linear building is part of the appeal.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
blurb: Cathedral built by Jesuits in 1613-1618 and made a cathedral in 1870; the Gëlle Fra golden lady stands nearby.

name: The Tube
blurb: Underground-themed bar with an international young crowd; very busy on Friday and Saturday nights.

name: Crossfire
blurb: Small, friendly Scandinavian-style pub just off Avenue de la Liberté.

name: Mousel's Cantine
blurb: Luxembourgish plates such as pork knee with broad beans, washed down with Mousel lager on the old brewery site.

name: Casa Museo Miguel de Unamuno
blurb: House museum for the Basque writer Miguel de Unamuno, who lived here in exile. Free entry.

name: Corralejo Sand Dunes
blurb: Golden dunes beside Corralejo for walking; dune-buggy rides are also offered.

name: Isla de los Lobos
blurb: Nature reserve island reached by a roughly 15-minute glass-bottom ferry from Corralejo harbour.

name: Oasis Park
blurb: Animal park with a children's play area and a café that is open all year.

name: Villa Winter
blurb: Private museum at Cofete, run on a voluntary entrance fee.

name: Caves of Ajuy
blurb: Caves near the fishing village of Ajuy, close to its black-sand beach.

name: Playa de Sotavento
blurb: Sandy beach named in the Fuerteventura listings. Beaches are public, so there is no entry fee.

name: El Campanario Canarian market
blurb: Corralejo shopping centre with a Canarian market every Sunday.

name: Morro Jable town centre
blurb: Town centre of Morro Jable, listed as open until late.

name: Bedrock Bar
blurb: Corralejo bar with a wide menu at reasonable prices. Book ahead for the Sunday roast.
